name: Zeely
tagline: Mobile-first AI tool that turns product photos and a short brief into short-form video ads and campaign creatives for small businesses.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The core loop here is not exotic: take a product image and a one-line brief, get a script, get a voiceover, composite it over stock or generated footage in a vertical frame, export. An agent can wire that with Remotion and FFmpeg and a couple of API keys in a weekend, and the output will be recognisably the same genre of video. What you will not reproduce in a sitting is the template library that makes the output not look like a school project, the mobile capture-to-post flow, or the ad-account plumbing. If you only need a few ads a month for your own shop, the DIY route is genuinely fine. If you need volume and variants that pass as professional, the templates are most of what you are actually buying.
coreLoopDIY: Takes product photos plus a short brief, has an LLM write a hook-and-CTA script, generates a voiceover, and renders a 9:16 captioned video over your assets with FFmpeg.
requirements: An LLM API key for scriptwriting
A TTS API key for voiceover, or record your own
Your own product photos or short clips, plus any licensed stock you want to use
whatYouLose: A curated template and motion library, which is the difference between an ad and a slideshow
The phone app: shooting, editing and posting from one place
Direct publishing and any ad-account or campaign integration
Whatever performance heuristics they have baked into their layouts and hooks
Someone else keeping up with platform aspect ratios, safe zones and format churn
moatNotes: Templates and motion design are labour, not technology. That labour is the product.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the hard part of ad creative is taste at volume, not video encoding. A self-built renderer gives you one look, and after the third ad everyone can tell. People pay for a bank of layouts that already look current, a phone workflow that fits between other tasks, and the absence of a render pipeline they personally have to debug at 11pm before a launch.
notes: Your first DIY ad will look fine and your tenth will look identical to your first, which is the whole argument for paying someone.
prompt:
Build a local CLI tool called adkit that generates short vertical video ads from product assets.

Stack, no substitutions: TypeScript on Node 20, Remotion for composition and rendering, system FFmpeg for audio muxing, Zod for config validation. No web UI, no database, no accounts, no telemetry.

Project layout:
- /assets: user drops product images and optional mp4 clips here
- /briefs: one JSON per ad, validated with Zod (product name, one-line value prop, target audience, tone, call to action, optional price)
- /src/remotion: compositions
- /out: rendered mp4s

Pipeline, run as `npm run ad -- briefs/foo.json`:
1. Load and validate the brief.
2. Call the LLM (OpenAI API, model and key from .env) to produce a strict JSON script: a 3 to 5 second hook line, two body beats, one CTA line, plus a suggested on-screen caption per beat. Retry once on invalid JSON.
3. Call a TTS API (ElevenLabs, key from .env) to render the voiceover to a wav per beat. If TTS_DISABLED=1, skip audio and render silent.
4. Render a 1080x1920 Remotion composition: Ken Burns pan on stills, hard cuts between beats, burned-in captions with a readable font and safe-zone padding, beat timing driven by the voiceover durations.
5. Mux voiceover plus an optional background track from /assets/music with FFmpeg, ducking music under speech with a fixed gain.
6. Write /out/{slug}-{timestamp}.mp4 and a sidecar JSON with the script used.

Ship exactly three visual templates (clean-product, before-after, testimonial-caption) selectable in the brief. Add `npm run ad -- briefs/foo.json --variants 3` to re-render the same script across templates.

Out of scope, do not build: social publishing, ad account APIs, scheduling, stock footage search, background removal, any hosted service.

Include .env.example, a README with the FFmpeg install line, and one committed example brief plus a placeholder image so `npm run ad` works immediately after keys are set.
